subject: test-planner
reason: Split by layer: the API filter rules (AC5) are e2e cases against the test stack when they need seeded orders, and functional cases for the 400 rejections (unknown, empty, numeric status); the page behaviour (AC1–AC4, AC6) is one e2e case per criterion branch, using an ordst-1 scenario with alice's Paid, Shipped and Cancelled orders and bob with none.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status=Paid returns only alice's two Paid orders, each as the unfiltered request returns it
covers: AC5: returns only that shopper's orders in that status
AC5: each as the unfiltered request returns it
items.reason: AC5 is the API contract the page depends on: a status filter must drop the orders in other statuses and must not change how the remaining ones are represented. It runs on the test stack because the Ordering functional host cannot hold saved orders; alice has orders in three statuses so a filter that ignores `status` would fail.

items.title: GET /api/orders without status still returns all four of alice's orders
covers: AC5: Without status it returns all of the shopper's orders, as today
items.reason: The new optional parameter must not change the existing unfiltered contract that the WebApp's "All" view and other clients use. A separate case because a regression here (for example defaulting to one status) would break every existing caller while filtered cases still pass.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status=sHiPpEd matches the status name ignoring case
covers: AC5: The name is matched ignoring case
items.reason: AC5 explicitly requires case-insensitive matching; a strict comparison would answer 400 for a valid status. Mixed case (not just lower case) proves the comparison ignores case rather than special-casing one form. Runs on the test stack so the match has a real order to return.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status=Submitted returns an empty list when alice has no Submitted orders
covers: AC5: returns only that shopper's orders in that status (none in that status)
items.reason: A valid status that matches nothing must answer an empty list, not 400 and not the unfiltered list; the page's `No <name> orders.` message (AC4) depends on that. Separate from the 400 cases because "valid name, no match" and "invalid name" must be told apart.

items.title: bob's GET /api/orders?status=Paid does not return alice's Paid orders
covers: AC5: returns only that shopper's orders in that status
items.reason: AC5 limits the result to the caller's own orders. A new filtered query path is exactly where the buyer condition can be dropped (filtering by status alone), leaking other shoppers' orders. Runs on the test stack with real orders owned by alice.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status=Delivered answers 400 with a problem detail
covers: AC5: A status that is not one of the six names answers 400 with a problem detail
items.reason: AC5 requires an unknown name to be rejected rather than ignored (which would silently return every order) or matched to nothing (which would return `[]`). The rejection happens before any order is read, so the cheaper functional layer (Ordering.API in-process against real Postgres) covers it.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status= (empty value) answers 400 with a problem detail
covers: AC5: A status that is not one of the six names answers 400 with a problem detail (empty value)
AC5: Without status it returns all (absent, not empty)
items.reason: The boundary between "no `status`" (all orders, AC5) and "a `status` that is not one of the six names" (400) is the empty value; read literally, an empty string is not one of the six names. Model binding easily turns `?status=` into null and returns everything, so this needs its own case. Functional because no order is read.

items.title: GET /api/orders?status=4 (numeric value of Paid) answers 400 with a problem detail
covers: AC5: A status that is not one of the six names answers 400 with a problem detail (numeric value)
items.reason: `OrderStatus` is an enum with numeric values (Paid = 4); a plain `Enum.TryParse` accepts `"4"` and would filter by Paid even though `4` is not one of the six names AC5 accepts. Functional because the rejection precedes any read.

items.title: My orders shows a "Status" filter with All and the six names in order, All selected
covers: AC1: Status filter above the list
AC1: options in order
AC1: All selected when the page opens
items.reason: AC1 fixes the filter's label, its seven options and their order, and the initial selection. Only the rendered WebApp shows these, so e2e; alice has orders, which AC1 requires for the filter to appear.

items.title: Choosing "Paid" shows only the Paid orders, unchanged, and the address becomes /user/orders?status=Paid
covers: AC2: choosing a status shows only my orders in that status
AC2: same columns and order as today
AC2: address becomes /user/orders?status=<name>
AC6: columns, totals, status badges unchanged
items.reason: The core user flow of the story: choose a status, see only matching orders rendered exactly as in the full list, with a shareable URL. Comparing against the unfiltered rows in the same test catches changed columns, totals, badges or ordering (AC6). Two Paid orders are needed to check their relative order.

items.title: Choosing "All" after a filter shows every order again at /user/orders
covers: AC2: choosing All shows every order again and the address is /user/orders
items.reason: AC2 requires "All" to clear the filter and drop the parameter entirely (not `?status=All` or `?status=`, which the API would reject). Starting from a filtered page proves the selection is undone, not just the initial state.

items.title: Opening /user/orders?status=Cancelled directly selects Cancelled and filters the list
covers: AC3: /user/orders?status=<name> opened directly selects that status and filters the list
items.reason: AC3 makes the filtered URL bookmarkable: the state must come from the address on first load, not only from clicking. Uses a different status than TC-ORDST-1-10 (Cancelled) so a page that only ever filters by Paid would fail.

items.title: Opening /user/orders?status=Delivered shows every order with "All" selected
covers: AC3: A status that is not one of the six names shows every order with All selected
items.reason: AC3 says an invalid page parameter degrades to the full list instead of an error; since the API answers 400 for unknown names (AC5), a page that passed the value through would show an error. E2e because only the rendered page shows the fallback.

items.title: A status none of alice's orders has shows "No StockConfirmed orders." and a "Show all orders" link
covers: AC4: status none of my orders has shows "No <name> orders." instead of the list
AC4: link "Show all orders" to /user/orders
AC4: filter still shown for a shopper with orders
items.reason: AC4 distinguishes "no orders in this status" from "no orders at all"; a page that showed "No orders yet" here would tell a shopper with four orders that they have none. Clicking the link checks it really leads back to the full list.

items.title: A shopper with no orders still sees "No orders yet" and no filter
covers: AC4: page for a shopper with no orders ("No orders yet") is unchanged and has no filter
AC1: filter only for a shopper with at least one order
items.reason: AC4 keeps the existing empty state and forbids the filter there; this also guards that a page with no orders and a status in the URL does not say "No Paid orders." instead. bob has no orders in scenario `ordst-1`, so he exercises it while alice's orders exist in the same database.

items.title: When a Paid order is shipped, the refreshed list keeps the Paid filter
covers: AC6: the list refreshing when an order's status changes
AC6: the refreshed list keeps the selected filter
items.reason: AC6 requires the existing live refresh to keep working and to keep the selected filter; a refresh that reloaded `/user/orders` would silently drop it and show all orders. Shipping order 101 through the Ordering API raises the real status-change event the WebApp listens to, so this needs the full test stack.
